text:
alice: Quick proposal — for the new quant8 candidate (q8-v3) I want a deterministic rollout gate that considers both quality deltas and latency regressions. idea: synthetic adversarial suite + production A/B checks.

sam: SGTM. can you sketch the gate rules? short bullets ok.

alice: sure. proposed gate: 1) local eval: no per-batch QA metric drop > 1.5% absolute on RMSE/QA_score across our core prompt suites (conv, extraction, summarization). 2) safety nets: null-safety (N/A responses) <= 0.3% relative increase. 3) latency: p95 +10ms allowed, p99 +25ms max. 4) canary: ramp 0.5% -> 5% over 12h if all pass. 5) auto-fallback: if production A/B shows quality delta > 1.0% (worse) on the tuned metric for two consecutive 1h buckets, route back to fp16.

kim: small Q: what is our "tuned metric" for this model? is it weighted QA_score or BLEU-like?

alice: tuned_metric = 0.55 * QA_score + 0.45 * extraction_f1. we weight precision-heavy tasks slightly higher for this customer cohort.

jordan: what about edge-case hallucination checks? we saw q8 earlier hallucinate on long-context less often but still spike on dates.

alice: add a targeted adversarial set (60 prompts) for hallucination/date stability. gate clause: no single adversarial subgroup drop > 2.0% absolute. if hit, block rollout.

sam: sounds good. can we make the fallback rule auto-trigger a canary-bot message + rollout reversal with reason code? I want the rollback to be fully auditable.

alice: yep — plan to use canary-bot to post: "rollback: q8-v3 -> fp16 due to quality_delta=1.2% on tuned_metric (2 x 1h buckets)" and attach last 5 failing prompts.

canary-bot: deploy-checklist: running local eval suite (234 cases) -> pass; starting staged ramp to 0.5% at 2026-03-18T10:42Z.

kim: one more: how do we prevent noisy signals (small sample variance) from tripping fallback? use Bayesian band/bootstrapping?

alice: yes — we use a bootstrap CI for the tuned_metric. fallback only if lower bound of 95% CI is worse than baseline by threshold (0.8%). also require consecutive buckets rule (2).

jordan: can we see the draft routing policy JSON?

alice: paste below:

```json
{
  "model": "q8-v3",
  "baseline_model": "fp16-v12",
  "ramp": [ {"percent": 0.5, "duration_h": 2}, {"percent": 2, "duration_h": 6}, {"percent": 5, "duration_h": 4} ],
  "gates": {
    "local_eval_drop_abs_pct": 1.5,
    "adversarial_subgroup_drop_abs_pct": 2.0,
    "null_safety_rel_pct": 0.3,
    "latency_p95_ms": 10,
    "latency_p99_ms": 25,
    "production_tuned_metric_delta_pct": 1.0,
    "ci_alpha": 0.05,
    "consecutive_buckets": 2
  },
  "auto_actions": {
    "on_failure": "rollback_to_baseline_and_alert",
    "snapshot_failures": 5
  }
}
```

sam: nice. two operational asks: 1) ensure model-compare logging includes prompt IDs and token counts; 2) add shadowing for 24h with full payloads for 1% of traffic before ramp.

alice: added both to rollout notes. shadowing + sample logs for the 1% cohort.

kim: how will this affect billing/cost? q8 is cheaper per token but we might double requests for shadowing.

alice: cost estimate: +1.2% overall due to shadowing, but expected net savings at 5% traffic stable. we have a cost cap metric in the console to alert if projected monthly spend delta > 3%.

jordan: any eval results yet vs fp16? numbers plz.

alice: local eval (full suite): tuned_metric delta = -0.4% (q8 worse), CI95 = [-0.9%, +0.1%] -> within CI. adversarial subgroup: one subgroup -1.7% (close to 2.0 threshold). latency: p95 +6ms, p99 +12ms. production 0% A/B (shadow only) small sample: tuned_metric delta = -0.9% (wide CI).

sam: risky but might pass with cautious ramp and the CI/consecutive rule. proceed with shadow+0.5% canary.

canary-bot: note: canary started at 0.5% at 2026-03-18T10:42Z. initial 30m bucket: sample=4200, tuned_metric_delta=-0.6%, CI95=[-1.3%, +0.1%].

kim: keep an eye on the adversarial subgroup — if that crosses -2.0% we stop. also watch null-safety.

alice: will monitor. I'll post hourly summaries and snapshot top 10 failing prompts if any gate trips.

sam: thanks — document the rollback playbook and add an incident template in #incidents in case automated rollback flips too often. :thumbsup:

alice: on it. tagging @jordan for postmortem template input.

jordan: happy to help.
